11/1/2026
Dear Records Custodian:

This is a public records request pursuant to Mass. Gen. Laws ch. 66, § 10A. I hereby request the following records.

I hereby request an excel/CSV extraction containing records of the following fields of information for all Boston Police Department employees from 6/1/2021 to 7/1/2021. Please include the following fields of information:
 
Employee first name
Employee last name
Employee middle name
Badge Number

I understand that you are not required to create a new public record to comply with my request, see, e.g., ch. 66, §6A(d), however, extraction of data from a database or electronic record system does not constitute creating a new record. See Att’y Gen. v. Dist. Att’y for Plymouth Dist., 484 Mass. 260, 275 (2021) (“[W]here public records are in electronic form, . . . a public records request that requires a government entity to search its electronic database to extract requested data does not mean that the extracted data constitute the creation of a new record under the public records law.”); see also 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(1)(f).

Please produce the records in an electronically-accessible format, including for screen readers, excel, or CSV. See 950 Mass. Code. Regs. 32.04(5)(d). Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf files or physical documents.

I request fees be waived as my request is in the public interest. See ch. 66, § 10(d)(v); 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.07(k). “All agencies and municipalities are strongly urged to waive fees associated with access to public records.” This request will contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department and is not in my commercial interest. Namely, these records will be made available to the public on Muckrock.com and will be used to update the Boston Police Index, a long-term community collaboration aimed to enhance transparency and accountability of the Boston Police Department through meticulous data collection and analysis. Thus, disclosure of these records will significantly contribute to the public’s understanding of the Boston Police Department’s operations.

If you do not waive the fees associated with my request, please provide a written, itemized, good faith estimate and explanation of the fees prior to fulfilling my request. See 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.0792)(b); see also ch. 66, § 10(e) (“A records access officer shall not charge a fee for a public record unless the records access officer responded to the requestor within 10 business days.”).

If you believe any of the records I have requested are exempt from disclosure, please identify both: (1) the records, categories of records, or portions of the records you intend to withhold; and (2) the specific reasons for such withholding, including the specific exemption you are relying on. See ch. 66, § 10(b)(iv).

If necessary to comply with my request, I welcome your suggested modifications pursuant to ch. 66, § 10(b)(vii) and 950 Mass. Code Regs. 32.06(2)(g). I am available to discuss any proposed modifications at (475)-243-3786 and mchristi@bu.edu

Thank you in advance for your time and attention to this matter. I look forward to receiving your response within 10 calendar days. See ch. 66, § 10(a).

Sincerely,
Michael Christie
BU SPARK!

I also request that, if appropriate, fees be waived as we believe this request is in the public interest, as suggested but not stipulated by the recommendations of the Massachusetts Supervisor of Public Records. The requested documents will be made available to the general public free of charge as part of the public information service at MuckRock.com, and is not made for commercial usage.

I expect the request to be filled in an accessible format, including for screen readers, which provide text-to-speech for persons unable to read print. Files that are not accessible to screen readers include, for example, .pdf image files as well as physical documents.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

ada sussman

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:
This is a request under the Massachusetts Public Records Law (M. G. L. Chapter 66, Section 10). I am requesting the following records:

1. Sheriff’s Department policies, memos or other guidance  currently in effect regarding communication and information sharing between departmental employees and a federal immigration authority, defined by M.G.L. Acts of 2026 C. 163 § 7 as “the United States Department of Homeland Security, United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement, United States Customs and Border Protection or any successor entity, and any person acting on their behalf.” The records request includes, but is not limited to, policies regarding:
A. Fingerprint and other data sharing with the above-named federal entities,
B. Guidance or policies concerning when communication with federal immigration authorities is allowed. This includes policies concerning how department employees can provide a federal immigration authority with nonpublic personal information, custody status, or advance notice of a person’s release from pretrial detention or upcoming court appearances. This also includes how and under what circumstances department employees are to document and respond to ICE detainer requests and other requests for information.

2. All Sheriff’s Department policies, guidance, memos or other records concerning the use of sheriff department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement. This includes policies concerning the use of sheriff department parking lots, facility interior, or exterior areas for immigration enforcement, staging, or the transfer of custody.  

3. All training materials the Sheriff’s Department has developed, used or trained employees on from September 4, 2026 through October 31, 2026 (or the date responsive records are collected for review if prior to October 31, 2026) regarding civil immigration enforcement, communication with federal immigration authorities, or the use of Sheriff’s department resources for federal civil immigration enforcement.

Pursuant to 950 CMR 32.07(2)(k), I request that your agency waive fees given that these records are in the public interest and I am not requesting this for commercial interests. Citizens for Juvenile Justice is an independent nonprofit organization working to reform youth serving systems statewide through Massachusetts. We engage in advocacy across the Commonwealth to ensure all youth are treated fairly and equitably regardless of their race, ethnicity, gender, gender identity, disability or immigration status. We plan to use these records to ensure that all people in Massachusetts, including youth, are adequately protected by law enforcement agencies regardless of real or perceived immigration status.  In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available.
The Public Records Law requires a written response within 10 business days. If you cannot comply with my request, you are statutorily required to provide an explanation in writing.

Sincerely,
Joshua Dankoff
Director of Strategic Initiatives 
Citizens for Juvenile Justice
joshuadankoff@cfjj.org

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. § 552, I respectfully request access to records maintained by U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP), a component of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), concerning U.S. entry restrictions, admissibility reviews, and interagency communications involving Mexican government officials, elected representatives, and political figures, including individuals affiliated with Mexico's National Regeneration Movement (Morena).

This request concerns official U.S. government actions and institutional coordination regarding restrictions affecting Mexican public officials.

I request records created or received between January 1, 2025, and November 2, 2026, including:

Existing administrative reports, statistical summaries, briefing documents, or internal assessments concerning restrictions on admission to the United States involving Mexican public officials, including governors, mayors, legislators, senior government officials, and political party leaders.

Official correspondence, memoranda, and interagency communications between CBP, the Department of State, and other DHS components concerning the implementation or coordination of entry restrictions affecting Mexican government officials.

Final policy guidance, administrative instructions, and memoranda concerning procedures used by CBP to implement visa-related restrictions, inadmissibility determinations, or entry limitations communicated by the Department of State or other federal agencies.

Existing aggregate statistical reports showing the number of Mexican nationals identified in official records as government officials or elected representatives who were subject to entry restrictions, inadmissibility determinations, or other relevant administrative measures, where such information is already compiled and can lawfully be disclosed.

Final internal briefing memoranda, official meeting summaries, and interagency coordination documents concerning restrictions affecting Mexican public officials in connection with corruption, organized crime, national security, or other statutory grounds of inadmissibility.

Records of official communications between CBP headquarters and U.S. government personnel assigned to Mexico concerning the implementation of entry restrictions affecting Mexican public officials.

Final or approved public affairs guidance, prepared questions and answers, and communications materials regarding public reporting about U.S. entry restrictions or visa cancellations involving Mexican political figures, including Morena-affiliated officials.

Please search, as appropriate, records maintained by:

CBP Office of Field Operations (OFO), including headquarters units responsible for admissibility and passenger programs.

CBP headquarters offices responsible for policy implementation and interagency coordination.

Other CBP offices reasonably likely to maintain responsive policy or administrative records.

Please provide responsive records electronically, preferably in searchable PDF format or their original electronic format where available.

If any records are withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemptions and release all reasonably segregable non-exempt information.

Hiroshi Takahashi

To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Dear FOIA Officer:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA), 5 U.S.C. § 552, I respectfully request copies of records held by the U.S. Department of State concerning the diplomatic response to the January 30, 2024, ProPublica investigation titled “Did Drug Traffickers Funnel Millions of Dollars to Mexican President López Obrador’s First Campaign?”, written by journalist Tim Golden.

The investigation described a previously undisclosed Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) inquiry into allegations of drug cartel contributions to Andrés Manuel López Obrador's 2006 presidential campaign.

Following publication, President López Obrador publicly accused U.S. government agencies of involvement in the disclosure, demanded an explanation and an apology from Washington, and questioned the implications for bilateral cooperation on migration, security, and counternarcotics.

I request records created or received between January 30 and September 30, 2024, including:

Internal correspondence, memoranda, and official communications between the Department of State, the U.S. Embassy in Mexico City, and relevant diplomatic offices regarding the publication of the ProPublica investigation and the Mexican government's response.

Diplomatic cables, situation reports, briefing memoranda, and assessments concerning the potential impact of the controversy on U.S.–Mexico bilateral relations.

Official correspondence, meeting summaries, and records of communications between U.S. diplomatic officials and representatives of the Mexican government addressing the allegations, the reported DEA investigation, or the Mexican president's requests for clarification or an apology.

Final or approved press guidance, talking points, prepared questions and answers, and internal communications concerning the U.S. government's public response to the controversy.

Records documenting whether U.S. officials assessed possible consequences for bilateral cooperation involving migration, border security, intelligence sharing, or counternarcotics operations.

Final briefing materials and meeting readouts prepared for senior Department of State officials or the U.S. Ambassador to Mexico concerning the diplomatic implications of the controversy.

Please search records maintained by the following offices, to the extent they are likely to possess responsive documents:

Bureau of Western Hemisphere Affairs (WHA).

U.S. Embassy Mexico City, including its Political Section.

Bureau of Global Public Affairs and relevant press offices.

Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL).

Office of the Secretary of State, where responsive records may exist.

Relevant search terms may include:

"Andrés Manuel López Obrador," "AMLO," "ProPublica," "Tim Golden," "DEA investigation," "2006 campaign," "Operation Polanco," "Mexico diplomatic relations," and "apology."

This request concerns the diplomatic and institutional response of the United States government to a publicly reported controversy. It does not seek confidential informant identities, protected personal information, or underlying DEA investigative files.

Please provide all reasonably segregable non-exempt portions of responsive records, including documents that may be partially redacted.

I request electronic delivery of the records.

Fee Classification and Public Interest Waiver

I am a journalist requesting these documents for news-gathering and public-interest reporting purposes.

I respectfully request classification under the news media fee category and a waiver of applicable fees, as disclosure would contribute significantly to public understanding of the diplomatic activities of the United States government and its relations with Mexico.

The requested information is not intended primarily for commercial use.

If any responsive records are withheld, please identify the applicable FOIA exemptions and release all reasonably segregable information.

Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,

Hiroshi Takahashi
